title: 484. The Food that Changed the World

sentences.en: Do you want to know what a pizza is?
sentences.zh: 你想知道什么是披萨吗？

sentences.en: It is a focaccia made from leavened bread dough, which is toasted in the oven.
sentences.zh: 它是一种用发酵面团做成的烤饼，在烤箱里烤制。

sentences.en: On top of it they put a sauce with a little bit of everything, when its hollas are combined.
sentences.zh: 当各种配料混合在一起时，他们在上面涂上一层百味俱全的酱汁。

sentences.en: The black of the toasted bread, the sickly white of the garlic, an anchovy, the greeny yellow of the oil and the fried greens, and the bits of red here and there from the tomato.
sentences.zh: 烤面包的焦黑、大蒜的病态白、一颗凤尾油鱼、橄榄油和炸青菜的青黄色，以及西红柿在这里和那里留下的红色碎块。

sentences.en: They make a pizza look like a patchwork of greasy filth that harmonizes perfectly with the appearance of the person that's selling it.
sentences.zh: 它们让披萨看起来像是一块油腻污秽的补丁，与卖披萨的人的外表完美契合。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, of course, was Hallo Holodi, the author of The Adventures of Pinocchio, and he was writing in 1886 about something called pizza.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，这个人当然就是哈洛·霍洛迪，《木偶奇遇记》的作者，他在1886年写到了一种叫做披萨的东西。

sentences.en: Beautiful accent, Tom.
sentences.zh: 漂亮的口音，汤姆。

sentences.en: Tuscan accent.
sentences.zh: 托斯卡纳口音。

sentences.en: Yeah, a Tuscan accent, which, of course, people familiar with the various dialects of Italy will have picked up from my dropping of the hard sea.
sentences.zh: 对，一种托斯卡纳口音，熟悉意大利各种方言的人当然会从我省略硬C音中听出来。

sentences.en: Did you notice that, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 你注意到了吗，多米尼克？

sentences.en: I did, I did, because Holodi was the son of a cook from Florence, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我注意到了，我注意到了，因为霍洛迪是来自佛罗伦萨的一个厨师的儿子，对吧？

sentences.en: So he took his food very seriously, took his Tuscan accent very seriously, and did not take pizza seriously.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常认真对待食物，非常认真对待他的托斯卡纳口音，却没有认真对待披萨。

sentences.en: He despised pizza.
sentences.zh: 他鄙视披萨。

sentences.en: Dominic, what do you think he would make of the global success today of pizza?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你觉得他会怎么看待今天披萨在全球取得的成功？

sentences.en: I think he'd be stupefied, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 我想他会被惊呆的，对吧？

sentences.en: He'd be appalled.
sentences.zh: 他会被吓坏的。

sentences.en: Do you think he'd be appalled?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他会被吓坏吗？

sentences.en: A patchwork of greasy filth.
sentences.zh: 一块油腻污秽的补丁。

sentences.en: I mean, I think his position is quite clear, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得他的立场相当明确，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess.
sentences.zh: 对，我猜是的。

sentences.en: I guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, we are not the people to ask about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们可不是问这个合适的人。

sentences.en: But fortunately, we're joined on the podcast by an old friend of the rest's history, the Professor of Italian Studies at University College London, John Dickey.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，伦敦大学学院意大利研究教授、历史学界的我们的老朋友约翰·迪基也加入了我们的播客。

sentences.en: Top Freemason expert.
sentences.zh: 顶级共济会专家。

sentences.en: Top Freemason expert, but also the author of Delizia, the epic history of Italians and their food.
sentences.zh: 顶级共济会专家，同时也是《美食帝国：意大利人及其食物的史诗历史》一书的作者。

sentences.en: John, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 约翰，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: What did you make of Tom's Tuscan accent, first of all?
sentences.zh: 首先，你觉得汤姆的托斯卡纳口音怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, I take all the blame because, of course, I tried to coach him in the rudiments of Tuscan pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我承担全部责任，因为我当然尝试过指导他托斯卡纳发音的基础知识。

sentences.en: But yeah, not a bad stab.
sentences.zh: 不过，嗯，尝试得还不错。

sentences.en: Even my laziest students will be encouraged now by those efforts.
sentences.zh: 现在，即使是我最懒的学生也会受到这些努力的鼓舞。

sentences.en: So, John, we're very glad to have you back on the podcast, not least because your great claim to fame,
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，我们很高兴你能重返播客，不仅因为你最出名的成就——

sentences.en: apart from being a top historian of Italy, is that you're the only person who's listened to all 11 episodes of the series about Custa and the Sioux.
sentences.zh: 除了作为意大利的顶级历史学家之外——你是唯一听完全部11集关于库斯塔和苏族系列节目的人。

sentences.en: Or as they would say in Tuscany, Husta.
sentences.zh: 或者正如他们在托斯卡纳所说的那样，胡斯塔。

sentences.en: Husta.
sentences.zh: 胡斯塔。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: The deep dive, the hour-by-hour narrative was excellent.
sentences.zh: 深入剖析、按小时讲述的叙事非常棒。

sentences.en: Oh, this is very good.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太棒了。

sentences.en: You can definitely come again.
sentences.zh: 你绝对可以再次光临。

sentences.en: So, I mean, your book is The Epic History of Italians and Their Food, and we're going to be condensing that epic history into the next 45 minutes to an hour or so.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你的书是《意大利人及其食物的史诗历史》，我们将把这段史诗般的历史浓缩到接下来的45分钟到一个小时左右。

sentences.en: I mean, an obvious point to make is that Italy, you know, it's a language not just of regional dialects,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个显而易见的观点是，意大利，你知道，它的语言不仅仅是区域方言，

sentences.en: or indeed, I guess you would have said regional languages before the 19th century, but regional cuisine.
sentences.zh: 或者说，我想在19世纪之前你可能会说是区域语言，但它是区域美食。

sentences.en: So is there even such a thing as Italian food?
sentences.zh: 所以甚至还存在意大利菜这种东西吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there is.
sentences.zh: 对，我认为是有的。

sentences.en: I mean, remember also that the regions are a relatively recent administrative invention in the 1970s, a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还要记住，大区是20世纪70年代一个相对较近的行政发明，其中许多都是如此。

sentences.en: We're talking about much more complicated patterns of diversity than that.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是比那复杂得多的多样性模式。

sentences.en: You know, if you think of Naples, Naples is the capital of a whole kingdom, essentially carved out by the Normans in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你想想那不勒斯，那不勒斯是一个完整王国的首都，基本上是由诺曼人在11世纪开创的。

sentences.en: And that makes its cuisine have a different shape to the cuisine of, you know, the central areas of Italy, or indeed Rome as the capital of the papacy.
sentences.zh: 这使得它的美食形态不同于意大利中部地区的美食，或者作为教皇国首都的罗马的美食。

sentences.en: So even the idea of Italian food as regional is a very simplistic map.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使是将意大利菜视为区域性的这种想法也是一张非常简单化的地图。

sentences.en: But I would say, yes, Italian food does exist, and it exists in the form of a kind of dialogue between cities, really.
sentences.zh: 但我要说，是的，意大利菜确实存在，它以城市之间某种对话的形式存在，真的。

sentences.en: Italian food is city food.
sentences.zh: 意大利菜就是城市菜。

sentences.en: That's my argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的论点。

sentences.en: Because I think the general sense, which is definitely one fostered by adverts, is the idea that Italian food comes from the country,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为普遍的看法——这绝对是广告所宣扬的一种看法——是意大利菜来自乡村，

sentences.en: and it's the mama with her traditional recipes, and that it's these recipes that have now been picked up by people in cities and kind of spread around the world.
sentences.zh: 是带有传统食谱的妈妈，现在城市里的人们采纳了这些食谱并在世界各地传播开来。

sentences.en: But you say that's not the case at all.
sentences.zh: 但你说根本不是这么回事。

sentences.en: There's a paradox here, because I think one of the reasons why Italian food has become so successful is because Italians are so devoted to believing that kind of nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个悖论，因为我认为意大利菜之所以如此成功的原因之一，是因为意大利人非常热衷于相信这种无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But there's really no evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 但真的没有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: You know, this sort of, you know, Italian peasants playing football in the olive grove version of Italian history, you may remember that ad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种，你知道的，意大利农民在橄榄树林里踢足球的意大利历史版本，你可能还记得那个广告。

sentences.en: All the documentation we have tells us that Italian peasants ate incredibly badly throughout history.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的所有文献都告诉我们，意大利农民在整个历史上都吃得极差。

sentences.en: You know, when Italy was unified in 1861, one of the first things they tried to do was find out more about the peasantry and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当1861年意大利统一时，他们试图做的第一件事就是更多地了解农民等等。

sentences.en: There's a sort of avalanche of documentation over the next 60, 70 years, and it all comes to the conclusion that the peasants not only ate badly,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的60、70年里，有海量的文献，它们都得出一个结论：农民不仅吃得差，

sentences.en: but didn't even know how to cook the few things they had to eat.
sentences.zh: 甚至连仅有的几样食物都不会做。

sentences.en: The fact that the average height of the Italian grew by four centimetres from the late 50s to the mid 70s,
sentences.zh: 从50年代末到70年代中期，意大利人的平均身高增长了四厘米，

sentences.en: when the economic miracle happened and that long, long history of peasant hunger came to an end, tells you something about how we misperceive Italian food history.
sentences.zh: 当时经济奇迹发生，那段漫长而又漫长的农民饥饿历史结束了，这向你说明了一些关于我们如何误解意大利饮食史的事情。

sentences.en: Just following up on that, cities in Italy go back to the Roman period.
sentences.zh: 顺着这一点说，意大利的城市可以追溯到罗马时期。

sentences.en: Is it possible to trace a history of Italian food back through the fall of the Roman Empire to the Roman period or not really?
sentences.zh: 是否有可能通过罗马帝国的衰落将意大利饮食史追溯到罗马时期，还是不太可能？

sentences.en: I don't think so, because I tried to do it and you can't.
sentences.zh: 我认为不可能，因为我试过这样做，但做不到。

sentences.en: Remember, some of them, some of those cities, particularly in the south, are older.
sentences.zh: 记住，其中一些城市，特别是南方的城市，历史更悠久。

sentences.en: You know, Messina is older than Rome itself and Naples and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，墨西拿比罗马本身还要古老，那不勒斯等等也是如此。

sentences.en: The Greek cities of the southern islands.
sentences.zh: 南方岛屿的希腊城市。

sentences.en: So what the classical world has bequeathed to contemporary Italy is what they call the hundred cities of Italy, these local centres with a very strong sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 所以古典世界留给当代意大利的是他们所说的意大利百城，这些地方中心具有极强的认同感。

sentences.en: You know, there are so many Italian dishes that carry the names of cities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有那么多带有城市名称的意大利菜肴。

sentences.en: Pizza alla Napoletana, bistecca alla Fiorentina, risotto alla Milanese, and so on and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 那不勒斯披萨、佛罗伦萨牛排、米兰烩饭等等等等。

sentences.en: That tells you something about the way that these cities produced foods and almost gave them a sort of urban branding as they were exchanged with other cities.
sentences.zh: 这向你说明了这些城市生产食物的方式，并且在与其他城市交流时，几乎赋予了它们一种城市品牌塑造。

sentences.en: That's where Italian food history happens.
sentences.zh: 意大利饮食史就是从那里诞生的。

sentences.en: That's where the documents are and the stories and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 文件、故事等等都在那里。

sentences.en: So let's start with the first city you talk about, which actually is a perhaps unexpected city, which is Palermo, the capital of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们从你谈到的第一个城市开始，这实际上是一个也许意想不到的城市，也就是西西里岛的首府巴勒莫。

sentences.en: So you kick off in 1154 in the reign of Roger II, the kind of Norman-Arab-Byzantine fusion of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 所以你在1154年鲁杰罗二世统治时期开始，当时是西西里诺曼-阿拉伯-拜占庭的融合时期。

sentences.en: And you start here because this is the arrival of the one thing that everybody associates with Italian food, which is pasta, or rather dried pasta.
sentences.zh: 你从这里开始，因为这是每个人都与意大利食物联系在一起的东西的到来，那就是意大利面，或者更准确地说是干面条。

sentences.en: So the fact that it's dried pasta, not fresh, that's the key, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以它是干面条，而不是新鲜的，这是关键，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Pasta, which is not a word, you know, it just means dough or paste.
sentences.zh: Pasta这个词，你知道，它不只是一个词，它只意味着面团或糊状物。

sentences.en: And it only really comes to mean what we mean by pasta relatively recently.
sentences.zh: 直到相对较晚的时候，它才真正开始意味着我们现在所说的意大利面。

sentences.en: And what we mean by pasta includes all kinds of things like tortellini, which are little pies.
sentences.zh: 而我们所说的意大利面包括各种各样的东西，比如意大利饺子（tortellini），它们是小馅饼。

sentences.en: That's what they mean.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们的意思。

sentences.en: They're tiny little pies, filled pastas that are cooked by boiling lasagna.
sentences.zh: 它们是极小的馅饼，是通过煮千层面来烹制的夹馅意大利面。

sentences.en: And all of these have different histories.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都有不同的历史。

sentences.en: But the one that is most, if you like, identified with Italy, even by Italians, is the dried variety, the stuff that fills supermarket shelves made with durum wheat.
sentences.zh: 但最能被意大利人（甚至由意大利人自己）认同为意大利代表的，是干面条品种，也就是超市货架上用硬质小麦制作的那种。

sentences.en: And the first document that testifies to the arrival of that on Italian soil dates from Roger II's reign in Palermo in 1154.
sentences.zh: 而证明它来到意大利土地上的第一份文件可以追溯到1154年巴勒莫的鲁杰罗二世统治时期。

sentences.en: And it comes from a geographer, Ali Derizi was his name.
sentences.zh: 它来自一位地理学家，他的名字叫阿里·德里齐。

sentences.en: He was an Arabic-speaking geographer, part of this extraordinary fusion court of Roger II, you know, with Greeks, Jews, and Arabs, and Normans moving together to run this kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他是一位说阿拉伯语的地理学家，是鲁杰罗二世这个非凡融合宫廷的一部分，你知道，希腊人、犹太人、阿拉伯人和诺曼人一起共同管理这个王国。

sentences.en: And he was the sort of one of the intellectual stars of this court.
sentences.zh: 他是这个宫廷的知识明星之一。

sentences.en: And he was commissioned to produce a planisphere, a great sort of silver-domed map of the known world
sentences.zh: 他受委托制作一张平面球仪，这是一种巨大的、带有银色圆顶的已知世界地图，

sentences.en: as a sort of advert for Roger's power, and a book to go with it, which describes, you know,
sentences.zh: 作为鲁杰罗权力的某种广告，还有一本随附的书，其中描述了，你知道的，

sentences.en: everything from the sort of desert islands of Scotland in the north to the sort of sandblasted unknown of Africa.
sentences.zh: 从北部苏格兰的荒岛到沙尘暴肆虐的未知非洲的一切。

sentences.en: And when he gets close to the Palermo capital, he starts, obviously, to get into more detail, and he goes to a place called Trabilla, which is just along the coast from Palermo,
sentences.zh: 当他接近巴勒莫首都时，他显然开始进入更多细节，他去了一个叫特拉比拉的地方，它就在沿着巴勒莫海岸不远的地方，

sentences.en: which is a centre famous for its springs and river courses.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以其泉水和河流流经而闻名的中心。

sentences.en: There he says that there is, and he uses the term factory, I'm not, you know, my Arabic is non-existent, but it's definitely a centre of large-scale production for export.
sentences.zh: 在那里他说，有一个——他用了工厂这个词，我不知道，我的阿拉伯语不存在，但它绝对是一个用于出口的大规模生产中心。

sentences.en: Producing this stuff he calls itria, and that is still used as an Italian word for a particular
sentences.zh: 生产这种他称之为itria的东西，这个词在意大利语中仍然用来指代一种特定的

sentences.en: type of pasta called tria, and it is short bits of dried durum wheat spaghetti, which, according to this geographer, Ali Drizzi, is made in huge amounts and exported all over
sentences.zh: 被称为tria的意大利面，它是短段的干硬质小麦细面条，据这位地理学家阿里·德里齐说，这种面条被大量制作并出口到各地，

sentences.en: the place, particularly all up and down the coast of Italy from Genoa right round to Naples and so on.
sentences.zh: 特别是从热那亚一直到那不勒斯等地的意大利海岸上下。

sentences.en: And that's where it arrives, and it arrives there from somewhere in the eastern Mediterranean that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 这就是它到达的地方，它是从我们不知道的东地中海某个地方到达那里的。

sentences.en: There's a long history of noodles, Chinese noodles are thousands of years old, but if you really want to be terminologically specific about it, that's where pasta history really
sentences.zh: 面条有着悠久的历史，中国面条有几千年的历史，但如果你真的想从术语上具体说明，那是意大利面历史真正

sentences.en: kicks off.
sentences.zh: 开始的地方。

sentences.en: So, John, you mentioned Chinese noodles.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，你提到了中国面条。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the most famous myths about Italian food is that actually pasta comes from China
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于意大利食物最著名的神话之一是意大利面实际上来自中国

sentences.en: and is introduced by Marco Polo, but clearly if it's originating in Sicily, then that can't be the case.
sentences.zh: 并且是由马可·波罗引入的，但很明显，如果它起源于西西里岛，那就不是这样了。

sentences.en: Marco Polo's 150 years later, and we've already got pasta here.
sentences.zh: 马可·波罗晚了150年，而我们这里已经有了意大利面。

sentences.en: Marco Polo doesn't mention pasta or noodles.
sentences.zh: 马可·波罗没有提到意大利面或面条。

sentences.en: And actually interesting, although Marco Polo didn't introduce spaghetti to Italy, he did
sentences.zh: 事实上有趣的是，虽然马可·波罗并没有把意大利面引入意大利，但他确实

sentences.en: help introduce it to the United States, because that story was actually invented for the first
sentences.zh: 帮助把它引入了美国，因为这个故事实际上是在1929年首次由美国意大利面制造商协会在他们的行业杂志中虚构出来的。

sentences.en: time by the Pasta Manufacturers Association of the United States in their industry magazine in 1929.
sentences.zh: 这个故事，然后出于某种神秘的原因，在30年代流行起来并被拍成电影，等等，带有这个意大利面轶事。

sentences.en: This story, which then, for some mysterious reason, took off and got made into a movie in the 30s, and so on with this pasta anecdote.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中的原因在于，他们真的很想让意大利面不那么具有意大利特色，从而不那么油腻、地中海风情和外国味，让它更具普遍性，这样他们就能卖出

sentences.en: And I think the reason there is they really wanted to make pasta less Italian, so less greasy and Mediterranean and foreign, and to make it more universal so they could sell
sentences.zh: 更多到美国市场的产品。

sentences.zh: 我们猜是的。

sentences.en: The thing is flatbreads, people putting discs of dough onto hot stones, you know, that's so ancient that what's specific about it sort of vanishes into nothing almoSt.
sentences.zh: 重点是扁面包，人们把面团圆盘放在热石头上烤，你知道，这太古老了，以至于它的具体起源几乎消失得无影无踪。

sentences.en: But it does, in the 19th century, start to become associated again with this culture of eating in the street of these ragged Neapolitan masses.
sentences.zh: 但在 19 世纪，它确实开始重新与这种衣衫褴褛的那不勒斯大众的街头饮食文化联系起来。

sentences.en: And that's where people start to observe it in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 人们正是在 19 世纪中期开始注意到这一点的。

sentences.en: Alexandre Dumas, the Three Musketeers, author, is one of the first people to pick it up.
sentences.zh: 《三个火枪手》的作者大仲马是较早提及它的人之一。

sentences.en: And there we do start to get traces of tomato as well as bits of anchovy and stuff.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我们确实开始发现番茄以及鳀鱼碎之类的痕迹。

sentences.en: It's just upflavouring.
sentences.zh: 这只是为了增添风味。

sentences.en: And it's very, very much associated with the low city of Naples, the poorest, most overcrowded quarters of the city.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常强烈地与那不勒斯下层城市、该市最贫困、最拥挤的街区联系在一起。

sentences.en: And it's street food, but not in a good way.
sentences.zh: 这是街头小吃，但不是什么好意义上的街头小吃。

sentences.en: Can I ask you then about probably the most famous of all pizzas, the Pizza Margherita, which is actually named after a queen, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那我可以问你关于可能最著名的披萨——玛格丽塔披萨吗？它实际上是以一位王后的名字命名的，对吧？

sentences.en: So how does that come about?
sentences.zh: 所以这是怎么来的？

sentences.en: Okay, Naples in the 19th century inspires horror and disgust because of cholera.
sentences.zh: 好吧，19 世纪的那不勒斯由于霍乱而令人感到恐惧和厌恶。

sentences.en: Cholera arrives in Europe in the, I think, 1820s, 1830s.
sentences.zh: 霍乱在 19 世纪 20 年代、30 年代左右传入欧洲。

sentences.en: And Naples, because of its hygienic conditions, its overcrowding, its poverty and so on and so on, is particularly vulnerable to it.
sentences.zh: 而那不勒斯由于其卫生条件、过度拥挤、贫困等等原因，对它格外脆弱。

sentences.en: I think there are something like eight outbreaks in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我想它在 19 世纪爆发了大约八次疫情。

sentences.en: And that's why nobody would dream of eating pizza.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么没有人会做梦去吃披萨。

sentences.en: We began with the quote from Carlo Collodi, the author of The Adventures of Pinocchio, who, again, wrote about pizza.
sentences.zh: 我们以《木偶奇遇记》的作者卡洛·科洛迪的名言开篇，他也曾写到过披萨。

sentences.en: And he wasn't remotely the only one.
sentences.zh: 而且绝不仅他一个人这么写。

sentences.en: It's something absolutely abhorrent and disgusting and associated with the city of Naples.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对令人厌恶、反感并与那不勒斯这座城市联系在一起的东西。

sentences.en: And there was a huge outbreak of cholera in 1884 in Naples, very, very politically dangerous moment.
sentences.zh: 那不勒斯在 1884 年爆发了大规模的霍乱，这是一个非常非常危险的政治时刻。

sentences.en: The wealthy, the middle classes just abandoned the city.
sentences.zh: 富人和中产阶级直接抛弃了这座城市。

sentences.en: And the king of the day, King Umberto, with his wife, Margherita, went to the city.
sentences.zh: 当时的国王翁贝托和他的妻子玛格丽塔来到了这座城市。

sentences.en: Actually, Umberto first, Margherita, went a couple of days later when they were kind of rebuilding the city.
sentences.zh: 实际上是翁贝托先去的，玛格丽塔在几天后他们开始重建城市时才去。

sentences.en: To build on their popularity, Naples has always had a kind of monarchical feeling about it that continued for a long time.
sentences.zh: 为了树立声望，那不勒斯一直有一种强烈的君主制情结，这种情结持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: And part of Margherita's image, she was a highly fashionable, you know, there was even a fashion magazine named after in the period.
sentences.zh: 作为玛格丽塔公众形象的一部分，她非常时髦，你知道的，当时甚至有一本以她名字命名的时尚杂志。

sentences.en: She was a real lifestyle leader.
sentences.zh: 她绝对是一位生活方式的引领者。

sentences.en: And it seems that pizza required its name, Pizza Margherita, that is,
sentences.zh: 看起来披萨正是在那个时期左右，

sentences.en: around that time as a sort of city's homage to these monarchs who had actually visited the city in its hour of need.
sentences.zh: 为了向这些在城市危难时刻真正来访的君主表达这座城市的敬意，而被赋予了“玛格丽塔披萨”这个名字。

sentences.en: Isn't there a story that there's one guy, Raffaele Esposito, who runs a bakery in the Spanish Quarter and he makes three pizzas?
sentences.zh: 难道没有这样一个故事吗：有一个人在西班牙区经营一家面包店，名叫拉斐尔·埃斯波西托，他做了三种披萨？

sentences.en: One with white baked, one just with olive oil, and one with the classic, you know, mozzarella.
sentences.zh: 一种是烤白披萨，一种只加橄榄油，还有一种加了经典的马苏里拉奶酪。

sentences.en: And she liked number three, and that's how it got the name.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢第三种，这就是它得名的原因。

sentences.en: Is that true or is that an urban myth?
sentences.zh: 这是真的还是都市传说？

sentences.en: That's another complete fake story, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 恐怕这又是一个彻头彻尾的假故事。

sentences.en: One of the many, many, I mean, writing Italian food history is really like machine gunning anchovies in a tin.
sentences.zh: 诸多此类故事之一，我的意思是，写意大利美食史简直就像是在罐头里用机关枪扫射鳀鱼。

sentences.en: You know, there are so many of these myths around, and that is one of them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有太多这样的传言了，这就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there is the Pizzeria Brandi, a famous pizzeria in Naples, which has this letter,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，那不勒斯有一家著名的披萨店叫Brandi披萨店，里面保存着这样一封信，

sentences.en: which is supposedly the original of Queen Margherita saying, thank you for these lovely pizzas, and that's a fake.
sentences.zh: 据说是玛格丽塔王后的原信，信中说感谢这些美味的披萨，但那是假的。

sentences.en: Are you personally, are you able to visit Italy?
sentences.zh: 你个人能去意大利吗？

sentences.en: Like, if there's not an embargo against you or something, like stamping on all these.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果没有对你下禁令或者别的什么，比如去查禁所有这些言论的话。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, you've got the masons getting you, now you've got the Italian foodies.
sentences.zh: 对，先是石匠协会找你麻烦，现在又轮到意大利美食界了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我懂。

sentences.en: Those who've read the book will know it's got a higher body count than my history of the Mafia.
sentences.zh: 读过这本书的人都知道，里面的死亡人数比我的黑手党史还要多。

sentences.en: This book, Delizio, got made into a TV series in Italy, a six-part series, me presenting in it, seemed to go down very, very well.
sentences.zh: 这本书《Delizio》在意大利被拍成了电视节目，一个六集的系列，由我主持，反响似乎非常非常好。

sentences.en: I don't know why, but it's since become much, much more controversial,
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么，但它此后变得更具争议性了，

sentences.en: because one of the dogs that didn't bark of Italian food is people pinning political identity to Italian food.
sentences.zh: 因为意大利食物中没有引起注意的一个反常现象是，人们将政治认同强加给意大利食物。

sentences.en: And that's begun to happen with the current fascist nostalgic government trying to use this idea of Italy's traditional Mediterranean peasant food.
sentences.zh: 而当前怀念法西斯的政府试图利用这种意大利传统地中海农民饮食的概念，这种现象也开始出现了。

sentences.en: Which you're saying is an American idea?
sentences.zh: 而你却说这是一个美国的概念？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: So irony is piled on irony?
sentences.zh: 所以这是讽刺叠加着讽刺？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是。

sentences.en: So could I just ask you about the attitude of the fascists, so the original fascists, Mussolini, to food?
sentences.zh: 那我能问一下法西斯分子，也就是最初的法西斯分子墨索里尼对食物的态度吗？

sentences.en: Because he's actually not particularly interested in it at all.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上他对食物根本不怎么感兴趣。

sentences.en: No, no, the fascists didn't like food.
sentences.zh: 不，不，法西斯分子不喜欢食物。

sentences.en: They ideally would have reduced the Italian diet to olive stones and gristle if they could have done.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，他们理想中会把意大利人的饮食缩减到橄榄核和软骨。

sentences.en: The idea was that these Italians, there's new Spartans or something marching to a new Mediterranean empire.
sentences.zh: 当时的理念是，这些意大利人是新斯巴达人或者别的什么，正迈向一个新的地中海帝国。

sentences.en: And, you know, Mussolini, he had a gastroduodenal ulcer, which tortured him for most of his political life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，墨索里尼患有胃十二指肠溃疡，这折磨了他政治生涯的大部分时间。

sentences.en: And he didn't like being photographed eating, preferred to be the sportsman and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢被拍到在吃东西，更愿意表现得像个运动员等等。

sentences.en: They tried to promote rice.
sentences.zh: 他们试图推广大米。

sentences.en: They had a battle for grain as, you know, this idea of self-sufficiency, of Italian food production under fascism in preparation for this war that they wanted from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 他们发起了“小麦战”，你知道的，这是在法西斯统治下追求自给自足和意大利粮食生产的理念，以此为他们从一开始就想要的这场战争做准备。

sentences.en: And Italian food, particularly pasta,
sentences.zh: 而意大利食物，尤其是意大利面，

sentences.en: just didn't fit into that because one of the terrible secrets of Italian pastures would be pretty much impossible to have an Italian pasta culture on the scale without importing grain from places like the Crimea.
sentences.zh: 根本不符合这一点，因为意大利面食的一个可怕秘密是，如果不从克里米亚等地进口谷物，几乎不可能建立起这种规模的意大利面食文化。

sentences.en: You know, Garibaldi had played his little role in importing grain from the Crimea in the early 19th century when he was a sailor.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，加里波第在 19 世纪初当水手时，曾在从克里米亚进口谷物方面发挥过他的一小部分作用。

sentences.en: But the fascists do invent the idea of the cult of the rural housewife with her traditional recipes, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但法西斯分子确实发明了农村家庭主妇及其传统食谱的崇拜概念，对吧？

sentences.en: So that's where that comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个概念的来源。

sentences.en: That's the first time that we do start to get a bit of sort of rustic eating nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 那是我们第一次开始接触到一点乡村饮食怀旧情结。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of rustic pastoral forms of poetry and opera and so on going on before that.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，各种乡村田园形式的诗歌和歌剧等等一直在进行着。

sentences.en: But there's really very, very little trace of anybody being crazy enough to associate eating well with the countryside before the fascists start to do it.
sentences.zh: 但在法西斯分子开始这样做之前，几乎没有任何迹象表明有人会疯狂到把吃得好与乡村联系起来。

sentences.en: But even their efforts weren't terribly convincing.
sentences.zh: 但即使是他们的努力也不是特别令人信服。

sentences.en: You know, they put on a big show in Rome and set up this sort of rustic village, so-called, in the Circus Maximus in Rome as part of an exhibition of fascist culture in 1938.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在罗马大肆炫耀，在罗马的大竞技场建立了一个所谓的乡村村庄，作为 1938 年法西斯文化展览的一部分。

sentences.en: But of course, this rustic village had all of these cuisines from Rome, from Venice, from Milan.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这个乡村村庄里囊括了来自罗马、威尼斯、米兰的各种美食。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was an urban picture of Italy as what it is, a collection of urban cuisines.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这是一幅关于意大利的城市化画卷——它本质上就是各种城市美食的集合。

sentences.en: And so basically what happens then, I'm guessing,
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，接下来发生的事情基本上就是，

sentences.en: is that it is an urban idea of what the countryside should be that then starts to shape the countryside to conform to this urban vision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于乡村应该是什么样子的城市化构想，随后它开始塑造乡村来顺应这种城市愿景。

sentences.en: Is that what happens?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it starts to happen once you reach the plenty in the post-war period, the economic miracle.
sentences.zh: 是的，一旦你到了战后繁荣时期、经济奇迹时期，这种情况就开始发生了。

sentences.en: Italy goes very, very rapidly from being a peasant society to being an industrial society, late 50s, 60s, 70s.
sentences.zh: 在 50 年代末、60 年代和 70 年代，意大利非常迅速地从一个农民社会转变为一个工业社会。

sentences.en: And really the 1970s are a key decade in this.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 70 年代确实是其中的一个关键十年。

sentences.en: It's a very difficult decade for Italy.
sentences.zh: 对意大利来说，这是非常艰难的一个十年。

sentences.en: It's the years of lead, of terrorism, and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 那是铅色年代、恐怖主义以及各种类似事态的时期。

sentences.en: The state feels corrupt.
sentences.zh: 国家让人感觉腐败。

sentences.en: And also of environmental crises of various kinds.
sentences.zh: 同时还伴随着各种环境危机。

sentences.en: And it's in this period in the 1970s that you start to get rustic food nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 正是在20世纪70年代的这个时期，你开始看到对乡村食物的怀旧情绪。

sentences.en: And the idea of Italian food is this collection of ancient peasant traditions, almost all completely invented.
sentences.zh: 而意大利食物的理念则是将古代农民传统汇集一处，几乎全部都是凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: That's when that rustic nostalgia really hits home.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，这种乡村怀旧情绪真正深入人心。

sentences.en: And you get inventions like the biscuit brand, il molino bianco, the white mill.
sentences.zh: 于是便有了诸如饼干品牌“白磨坊”（il molino bianco）这样的发明。

sentences.en: Yeah, which is just totally fabricated.
sentences.zh: 没错，这完全是虚构出来的。

sentences.en: So I wanted to ask you about one person that you zero in on here, which is Giovanni Rana, if I pronounced that correctly.
sentences.zh: 所以我想问你关于你在这里重点关注的一个人，也就是乔瓦尼·拉纳（Giovanni Rana），如果我没念错名字的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He is the tortellini magnate.
sentences.zh: 他是意大利面王（tortellini magnate）。

sentences.en: So tortellini, if I understand you correctly, was a Sunday food.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我没理解错的话，意大利面（tortellini）曾是一种周日的食物。

sentences.en: You had it on Sundays and you had it in a broth.
sentences.zh: 你会在周日吃它，并且是用高汤煮着吃。

sentences.en: And there's sort of little pass, almost like dumplings, I guess.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像小口袋，差不多就像饺子一样，我想是的。

sentences.en: And he takes that and he makes it a convenience food with huge factories and stuff.
sentences.zh: 而他将这一点拿过来，通过巨大的工厂等设施把它变成了便捷食品。

sentences.en: But also the key to it is his marketing.
sentences.zh: 但关键也在于他的营销。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That he markets himself.
sentences.zh: 即他把自己作为活招牌进行营销。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what people miss out completely with this rustic traditions version of Italian history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是人们在看待意大利历史的这种乡村传统版本时完全忽略的地方。

sentences.en: There is the commercial genius that is behind contemporary success of Italian food.
sentences.zh: 在意大利食物当代成功的背后，存在着商业天才。

sentences.en: Tortellini are medieval.
sentences.zh: 意大利饺（Tortellini）是中世纪的产物。

sentences.en: They're very ancient.
sentences.zh: 它们非常古老。

sentences.en: They're these little pies.
sentences.zh: 它们就是这些小馅饼。

sentences.en: Medieval people loved a pie that you cook by boiling mini pie.
sentences.zh: 中世纪的人们酷爱一种通过水煮来烹制的迷你馅饼。

sentences.en: So they're very ancient.
sentences.zh: 所以它们非常古老。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are recipes right back into those medieval cookbooks we talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 而且，如你所知，早在我们刚才提到的那些中世纪食谱中就能找到它们的做法。

sentences.en: By the post-war period, period of prosperity, this sort of Sunday lunchtime treat in the brief historical existence of the classic Italian housewife.
sentences.zh: 到了战后繁荣时期，在传统意大利主妇短暂的历史存在中，这成了周日午餐的一种犒赏。

sentences.en: This is what they become in the post-war period.
sentences.zh: 这正是它们在战后时期的写照。

sentences.en: They've come from being part of the peasant labor force, moved into cities.
sentences.zh: 它们由最初的农民劳动力转变为进城务工人员。

sentences.en: I'm generalizing massively, obviously.
sentences.zh: 当然，我在做极大的概括。

sentences.en: And then they get pushed into education and into the labor market again.
sentences.zh: 然后他们再次被推向教育领域和劳动力市场。

sentences.en: And people can't make those things anymore, whether they don't have the skills or most certainly they don't have the time.
sentences.zh: 人们再也无法制作那些东西了，要么是因为缺乏手艺，要么更确定是因为没有时间。

sentences.en: And Giovanni Rana in the late 60s, 70s, 80s, seizes onto this.
sentences.zh: 而乔瓦尼·拉纳在60年代末、70年代和80年代抓住了这一点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because Tortellini present a huge problem of truSt.
sentences.zh: 因为意大利面带来了巨大的信任问题。

sentences.en: What is in the filling?
sentences.zh: 馅料里到底是什么？

sentences.en: You can put any old muck in there if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，你可以在里面塞进任何乱七八糟的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You've got to have truSt.
sentences.zh: 你必须建立信任。

sentences.en: And he puts his face on the packet,
sentences.zh: 于是他在包装袋上印上了自己的脸，

sentences.en: his signature on the packet to translate that trust into the era of vacuum packing and urban living and supermarket distribution and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 在包装袋上签上自己的名字，以此将这种信任转化为真空包装、城市生活、超市分销以及所有诸如此类事物的时代特征。

sentences.en: And they've become a huge success.
sentences.zh: 它们取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And if you buy packet Tortellini from Sainsbury's or whatever it is in Britain, they're almost certainly made by Giovanni Rana.
sentences.zh: 如果你在英国的森宝利（Sainsbury's）或其他什么地方买袋装意大利面，它们几乎可以肯定是乔瓦尼·拉纳生产的。

sentences.en: So, John, can we just end?
sentences.zh: 那么，约翰，我们能收尾了吗？

sentences.en: As you said, you've been shooting anchovies in a tin here.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你在这里简直是在瓮中捉鳖（轻易击碎了各种神话）。

sentences.en: There seem very few myths left.
sentences.zh: 似乎没剩下几个神话了。

sentences.en: And yet there is a sense that there is something distinctively appealing to a frenetic modern world about Italy and Italy's food culture, the idea of slow food.
sentences.zh: 然而人们依然觉得，对于狂热的现代世界而言，意大利和意大利的饮食文化——慢食的理念——有着某种独特的吸引力。

sentences.en: Is it all just marketing and American influence and whatever?
sentences.zh: 这一切都只是营销、美国影响以及诸如此类的东西吗？

sentences.en: Or is there something genuinely true about it, despite everything that you've been saying?
sentences.zh: 或者说，尽管你说了这么多，其中依然有某种真实不虚的东西？

sentences.en: I think that that connoisseurship that is associated with urban living in Italy, that we get developing the Middle Ages,
sentences.zh: 我认为，与意大利城市生活息息相关的那种鉴赏力，也就是我们在中世纪发展起来的鉴赏力，

sentences.en: wider selection people learning the manners and connoisseurship that go with good eating.
sentences.zh: 即更多样化的选择、人们学习与美食相伴的礼仪和鉴赏力。

sentences.en: That communicates itself and is in a position when people do have the resources then to rediscover and exploit these traditions, you know,
sentences.zh: 这种鉴赏力得以传播，当人们拥有资源时，便能够重新发现并利用这些传统，你知道的，

sentences.en: all kinds of advertising flummery about peasant traditions.
sentences.zh: 各种关于农民传统的广告浮夸之词。

sentences.en: And the slow food case is that language, that process turned into politics, effectively, the politics of food.
sentences.zh: 而慢食运动的观点则是，将那种语言和过程转化为政治，实际上就是食物政治。

sentences.en: And Carlo Petrini, a great friend of our current king, is the founder of this movement, found in the 80s as a sort of rebellion against fast food and the commercialization of food.
sentences.zh: 卡洛·佩特里尼（Carlo Petrini）是我们现任国王的挚友，他是这个运动的创始人，于80年代创立了该运动，作为对快餐和食物商业化的一种反叛。

sentences.en: So it's in Italy too, because the memory of peasant existence really wasn't that, you know, it was only a generation ago.
sentences.zh: 所以在意大利也是如此，因为对农民生活的记忆其实并非那么遥远，你知道的，那只是一个世代前的事。

sentences.en: The Italians start to capitalize that in a commercial way with the kind of commercial know-how.
sentences.zh: 意大利人开始以商业方式，借助某种商业诀窍，将这一点资本化。

sentences.en: So the myths are mostly entirely mythical, but they do in a sense misapprehend a history, which they can then put to very good commercial use.
sentences.zh: 因此这些神话在很大程度上完全是虚构的，但从某种意义上说，它们确实误解了一段历史，而他们随后能将这段历史付诸极好的商业利用。

sentences.en: And the fact remains, I mean, you've got a statistic in your book that there are 10 times fewer fast food outlets, burger outlets or whatever,
sentences.zh: 但事实依然摆在那里，我是说，你的书中有一个统计数据：

sentences.en: in Italy than there are in Britain or France or Germany.
sentences.zh: 意大利的快餐店、汉堡店或其他类似店铺的数量比英国、法国或德国少10倍。

sentences.en: So Italy are the outliers.
sentences.zh: 所以意大利是个特例。

sentences.en: I was thinking about what makes Italy different.
sentences.zh: 我在思考是什么让意大利与众不同。

sentences.en: And I guess you could argue what makes Italy different is that it always had that network of cities and that that was the distinctive thing about it.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以辩称，让意大利与众不同的是它一直拥有那个城市网络，而这正是它独特的地方。

sentences.en: France obviously has Paris and it has other major cities, but it doesn't have quite the same competitive world of city-states.
sentences.zh: 法国显然有巴黎和其他主要城市，但它并没有完全相同的相互竞争的城邦世界。

sentences.en: Is that the thing?
sentences.zh: 是这个原因吗？

sentences.en: Is that what makes Italy different?
sentences.zh: 这就是让意大利与众不同的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: Italy's long food history, most Italians simply weren't a part of for so long.
sentences.zh: 意大利悠久的饮食历史，绝大多数意大利人在很长一段时间里根本没有参与其中。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, bequeathed the sort of aspirations and a model for sophisticated eating, urban living, which, you know, is still very strongly felt in Italy.
sentences.zh: 然而，它留下了对精致饮食、城市生活的种种追求与典范，你知道的，这在意大利依然有着强烈的回响。

sentences.en: This sense of living amid these ancient stones and these artistic treasures and food has been kind of bolted onto that.
sentences.zh: 这种身处古老石砌建筑和艺术珍品之中的生活感，而食物则像是附加在这一切之上的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, I should say that Italy is vulnerable to a lot of these trends.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我应该指出意大利很容易受到许多此类潮流的影响。

sentences.en: Apparently, Italians now eat more sushi per head than anybody else in the world.
sentences.zh: 显然，现在意大利人按人均计算吃掉的寿司比世界上任何其他地方的人都多。

sentences.en: And I don't know why it is that sushi made such a big impact in Italy, but Italians absolutely love it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么寿司在意大利产生了如此巨大的影响，但意大利人绝对对其喜爱有加。

sentences.en: You know, John,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，约翰，

sentences.en: the peak delicacy in the Roman period for the elite was to eat kind of fish that was almost raw because you could only have it if it was fresh from your ponds or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在罗马时期，精英阶层的巅峰美食就是吃那种几乎是生鱼的鱼，因为只有当你池塘里现捞或诸如此类最新鲜的时候，你才能吃到它。

sentences.en: So it was an absolute marker of status.
sentences.zh: 所以这是地位的绝对标志。

sentences.en: So perhaps it's a reversion to their very ancient ruins.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这是对他们远古废墟的一种回归。

sentences.en: I like to think that that's what it is.
sentences.zh: 我愿意相信事实就是如此。

sentences.en: Anyway, John, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 总之，约翰，非常感谢。

sentences.en: That was absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这真的是太精彩了。

sentences.en: And it's lunchtime now.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是吃午饭的时间了。

sentences.en: Now I might pop out to Brixton Hill and go to Pizza Brixton, upholding the Dolce Vita in South London.
sentences.zh: 现在我可能会顺道去布里克斯顿山（Brixton Hill）的布里克斯顿披萨店，在伦敦南部发扬甜蜜生活（Dolce Vita）精神。

sentences.en: So John's book, as a reminder to you all, is Delizia, the epic history of Italians and their food.
sentences.zh: 因此，再次提醒各位，约翰的书是《美味：意大利人及其食物的史诗历史》（Delizia, the epic history of Italians and their food）。

sentences.en: John, brilliant to have you back on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 约翰，很高兴你能再次作客本播客。

sentences.en: At some point, we'll definitely have you back to do the Mafia so that you really can block your copybook in Italy.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，我们一定还会请你来聊聊黑手党，这样你就能彻底在意大利名誉扫地了。

sentences.en: Just to say, you know, anyone who's going to Italy, it's an absolutely wonderful book to take and read.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，任何要去意大利的人，这绝对是一本极佳的随身读物。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来参加。

sentences.en: And thank you all for listening.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Ciao.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 再见。
